raw_response:
I will mostly do what has worked on my land, then adjust a little for cost and water. I have 11.4 mu, so I am not farming tiny area, but I still count every bag. Wheat and maize are my main stomach crops and cash support, so I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize cycle and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Around here, if I cut fertilizer too much and the stand turns weak, I cannot make that yield back later, so I would rather spend a bit more on base fertilizer than lose production. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage on wheat and maize, especially at the key times. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize and cotton seed, because after so many years I have seen clearly that the better seed gives a more even stand and better yield if I feed it properly.

For this year, I will put 8.4 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and 3.0 mu into cotton. On wheat, I will not be stingy: I will feed it enough at sowing and again at jointing, and I will water about three times if the season is normal. On maize, I will go with hybrid seed and keep fertilizer mainly for early growth and the big-mouth stage, with two irrigations if rain is not enough. Cotton takes more watching and more spraying, but I still keep some because I know how to manage it and it spreads my risk a bit. I will plough the cotton ground, use rotary for wheat land, and use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat to save time and labor.
